Check visible duplication/variant drift/incentives/documented manipulation. Detail, stars, badges or AI detectors cannot certify truth/fakery; incentives are not automatic falsity. Separate usefulness/credibility.

Keep three questions apart: whether a seller's review display can be audited, whether each review reflects a real buyer, and whether the product works; an answer to one settles neither of the others. Record each review's provenance (seller-curated, embedded testimonial, independent platform, imported or syndicated, email- or order-verified, incentivized, unknown) and compare displayed totals with the texts actually read; a failed "load more" or an empty review feed is an access boundary, not evidence of fabrication. Before reading a cross-platform mismatch as manipulation, check imports, order-ID eligibility, earlier product IDs and migrated testimonials. Weigh specific firsthand reports (symptom or function, duration, co-exposures, stop and restart, objective measures) above content-free praise, in both directions: they can raise the probability that some buyers benefit, never establish how many or how much. A questionable review practice and a working product are compatible.
